question.prompt: There are \(120\) seats in a row. What is the fewest number of seats that must be occupied so the next person to be seated must sit next to someone?

solutions.explanation:
We need every empty seat to have an occupied neighbor. Imagine marking each occupied seat and its immediate neighbors. Any unmarked seat would be empty with no occupied neighbor, so all \(120\) seats must be marked.

Each occupied seat marks at most three seats. With \(39\) or fewer occupied seats, at most
\[
3\cdot39=117
\]
seats can be marked. Overlapping marks can only reduce that number. Thus at least \(40\) seats must be occupied.

To show that \(40\) works, divide the row into \(120\div3=40\) consecutive groups of three and occupy the middle seat in every group. These are seats \(2,5,8,\ldots,119\). Every empty seat is beside the occupied seat in its group, including seats \(1\) and \(120\). Therefore the fewest occupied seats is \(40\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Cover the row in groups of three
